title: How Reliable Are Open-Access Lung Nodule Segmentation Models? Agreement with Radiologists, Repeatability, and Classification at CT
summary: Among eight configurations of seven open-access lung nodule segmentation methods tested in 10 CT datasets, a method given one point returned a mask for every nodule, but none matched agreement between five radiologists on radiomic features.
key_points: In this retrospective study of 10 CT datasets, the three methods given no point prompt returned masks for 0.5% (5 of 1098) to 51.3% (563 of 1098) of nodules 8 mm or smaller.

On CT repeated minutes apart in 28 patients with large lung tumors (median diameter, 38 mm), radiomic feature repeatability with nnInteractive masks was close to that with manual contours (median intraclass correlation coefficient difference, 0.003 [95% confidence interval: −0.006, 0.012]).

In a screening dataset of 2487 nodules, the best radiomic model (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.72 [95% confidence interval: 0.68, 0.76]) did not exceed nodule diameter (0.73 [95% confidence interval: 0.69, 0.76]) and was below the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System category (0.83 [95% confidence interval: 0.79, 0.87]).

abstract.Purpose: To evaluate whether open-access lung nodule segmentation methods are reliable for quantitative CT beyond segmentation accuracy.
abstract.Materials and Methods: In this retrospective study of 10 CT datasets, eight configurations of seven methods ran with published weights, and point prompts marked reference nodule centers. Metrics were Dice similarity coefficient; radiomic feature concordance with radiologists minus inter-reader concordance (Δ; prespecified margin, −0.05, in a five-reader dataset); test–retest intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); and classification area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
abstract.Results: Included were 12726 nodules in 6715 patients (mean age ± SD, 62 years ± 10; 3018 of 6014 [50.2%] women). nnInteractive segmented all 4075 nodules with a reference segmentation (median Dice, 0.77); methods without a location segmented 0.5%–51.3% of 1098 nodules 8 mm or smaller. In the five-reader dataset, nnInteractive had the smallest Δ (−0.037 [95% CI: −0.066, −0.017]) but missed the margin (*P* = .94). MedSAM2 had median Dice of 0.82 (nnInteractive, 0.84) but shape-feature Δ of −0.204 (nnInteractive, −0.027). In 28 same-day CT pairs of large tumors, median ICC with nnInteractive differed from manual contours by 0.003 (95% CI: −0.006, 0.012). Classification AUCs with nnInteractive masks were 0.000 (95% CI: −0.009, 0.009) to 0.027 (95% CI: 0.005, 0.049) lower than with reference masks.
abstract.Conclusion: A point-prompted method agreed less with radiologists on radiomic features than radiologists did with one another but was close to manual contours in repeatability and classification; similar Dice did not mean similar features, and methods without a location missed many small nodules.

limitations: This study had limitations. First, most multireader nodules were in methods' training data, and QIBA, the only multireader dataset outside it for most methods, had 52 nodules outlined with semiautomated software, so agreement may be overstated. Second, points were placed at the reference center, so point-prompted results are upper bounds. PiNS also received the nodule extent and was developed by an author. Third, repeatability was measured in 28 large tumors whose scans two methods had seen, not in screening nodules. Fourth, suspicion labels in LIDC-IDRI and LNDb came from the readers who drew the masks, screening labels were per patient, and classification had no external test. Fifth, IMD-CT was excluded and then reinstated after results were known, and no method or reference measured the solid component of part-solid nodules. Finally, apart from the QIBA test, all hypothesis tests were added after the results were known.
data_availability: All 10 datasets are available as described by their sources (Table 1): LIDC-IDRI (16), LNDb (17), QIBA (18), RIDER-Seg (19), IMD-CT (20), NSCLC-RG (21), QIN (33), LUAD-Surv (22), DLCS24 (23), and LUNA25-Dev (24). Masks, features, analysis code, the statistical analysis plan, and its change log will be released at [repository URL and DOI to be supplied]. Masks produced with weights under noncommercial licenses (nnInteractive, VoxTell, and MedSAM2) will be released under a noncommercial license; model weights are not redistributed.

quotes.coverage: Of 1098 nodules of 8 mm or less, TotalSegmentator returned masks for 51.3% (563 of 1098), VoxTell for 42.5% (467 of 1098), VISTA3D-Auto for 0.5% (5 of 1098), and nnInteractive for all (median Dice, 0.72) (Fig 3b).
quotes.dice_vs_features: Although QIBA median Dice was 0.84 for nnInteractive and 0.82 for MedSAM2 (Table S5), the gap in shape features was −0.027 (95% CI: −0.063, 0.004) and −0.204 (95% CI: −0.381, −0.043) (Appendix S2).
quotes.criterion: No configuration met the criterion (*P* = .94 for nnInteractive and *P* > .99 for the other prespecified configurations); with the −0.10 sensitivity margin, nnInteractive did (*P* ≤ .003).
